passages.text: Now the LORD attended to Sarah as He had said, and the LORD did for Sarah what He had promised.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
God remembered Sarah.
God had spoken about Sarah before.
God did for Sarah what He had promised.
God kept His word to Sarah.
passages.original: וַֽיהוָ֛ה פָּקַ֥ד אֶת־ שָׂרָ֖ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמָ֑ר וַיַּ֧עַשׂ יְהוָ֛ה לְשָׂרָ֖ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֵּֽר׃

passages.text: So Sarah conceived and bore a son to Abraham in his old age, at the very time God had promised.
passages.sermon:
Sarah was Abraham’s wife.
Abraham was very old.
God had promised Abraham a son.
Sarah became pregnant.
Sarah gave birth to a son for Abraham.
This happened at the exact time God had promised.
passages.original: וַתַּהַר֩ וַתֵּ֨לֶד שָׂרָ֧ה לְאַבְרָהָ֛ם בֵּ֖ן לִזְקֻנָ֑יו לַמּוֹעֵ֕ד אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבֶּ֥ר אֹת֖וֹ אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: And Abraham gave the name Isaac to the son Sarah bore to him.
passages.sermon: Abraham was the husband of Sarah.\r\nSarah gave birth to a son for Abraham.\r\nAbraham named his son Isaac.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶֽת־ שֶׁם־ בְּנ֧וֹ הַנּֽוֹלַד־ ל֛וֹ אֲשֶׁר־ יָלְדָה־ לּ֥וֹ שָׂרָ֖ה יִצְחָֽק׃

passages.text: When his son Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, as God had commanded him.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was Isaac’s father.
Isaac was eight days old.
God had commanded Abraham to circumcise his son.
Abraham circumcised Isaac.
passages.original: וַיָּ֤מָל אַבְרָהָם֙ אֶת־ יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֔וֹ בֶּן־ שְׁמֹנַ֖ת יָמִ֑ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה אֹת֖וֹ אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.
passages.sermon: Abraham was one hundred years old.\r\nIsaac was Abraham’s son.\r\nIsaac was born to Abraham when Abraham was one hundred years old.
passages.original: וְאַבְרָהָ֖ם בֶּן־ מְאַ֣ת שָׁנָ֑ה בְּהִוָּ֣לֶד ל֔וֹ אֵ֖ת יִצְחָ֥ק בְּנֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then Sarah said, “God has made me laugh, and everyone who hears of this will laugh with me.”
passages.sermon:
Sarah was Abraham’s wife.
Sarah spoke.
Sarah said, “God made me laugh.”
Everyone who hears about this will laugh with me.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר שָׂרָ֔ה צְחֹ֕ק עָ֥שָׂה לִ֖י אֱלֹהִ֑ים כָּל־ הַשֹּׁמֵ֖עַ יִֽצְחַק־ לִֽי׃

passages.text: She added, “Who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age.”
passages.sermon:
Sarah was Abraham’s wife.
Sarah spoke.
Sarah said, “Who would have told Abraham this?”
Sarah said, “Who would have said that Sarah would nurse children?”
Sarah said, “I have given Abraham a son in his old age.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֗אמֶר מִ֤י מִלֵּל֙ לְאַבְרָהָ֔ם הֵינִ֥יקָה בָנִ֖ים שָׂרָ֑ה כִּֽי־ יָלַ֥דְתִּי בֵ֖ן לִזְקֻנָֽיו׃

passages.text: So the child grew and was weaned, and Abraham held a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was a child.
Isaac grew older.
Isaac stopped nursing.
Abraham was Isaac’s father.
Abraham made a great feast.
Abraham held the feast on the day Isaac stopped nursing.
passages.original: וַיִּגְדַּ֥ל הַיֶּ֖לֶד וַיִּגָּמַ֑ל וַיַּ֤עַשׂ אַבְרָהָם֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֣ה גָד֔וֹל בְּי֖וֹם הִגָּמֵ֥ל אֶת־ יִצְחָֽק׃

passages.text: But Sarah saw that the son whom Hagar the Egyptian had borne to Abraham was mocking her son, and she said to Abraham, “Expel the slave woman and her son, for the slave woman’s son will never share in the inheritance with my son Isaac!”
passages.sermon:
Sarah was Abraham’s wife.
Hagar was an Egyptian slave woman.
Hagar had a son with Abraham.
Sarah saw Hagar’s son mocking.
Sarah spoke to Abraham.
Sarah said, “Expel this slave woman and her son.”
Sarah said, “The slave woman’s son will not share the inheritance with my son Isaac.”
passages.original: וַתֵּ֨רֶא שָׂרָ֜ה אֶֽת־ בֶּן־ הָגָ֧ר הַמִּצְרִ֛ית אֲשֶׁר־ יָלְדָ֥ה לְאַבְרָהָ֖ם מְצַחֵֽק׃ וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לְאַבְרָהָ֔ם גָּרֵ֛שׁ הָאָמָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את וְאֶת־ בְּנָ֑הּ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יִירַשׁ֙ בֶּן־ הָאָמָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את עִם־ בְּנִ֖י עִם־ יִצְחָֽק׃

passages.text: Now this matter distressed Abraham greatly because it concerned his son Ishmael.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was Isaac’s father.
Abraham was also Ishmael’s father.
Sarah told Abraham to send Hagar and Ishmael away.
This matter upset Abraham very much.
Abraham felt great distress because the matter was about his son Ishmael.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֧רַע הַדָּבָ֛ר מְאֹ֖ד בְּעֵינֵ֣י אַבְרָהָ֑ם עַ֖ל אוֹדֹ֥ת בְּנֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But God said to Abraham, “Do not be distressed about the boy and your maidservant. Listen to everything that Sarah tells you, for through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Abraham.
God said, “Do not be distressed about the boy Ishmael.
Do not be distressed about your maidservant Hagar.
Listen to everything that Sarah tells you.
Your descendants will be named through Isaac.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶל־ אַבְרָהָ֗ם אַל־ יֵרַ֤ע בְּעֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ עַל־ הַנַּ֣עַר וְעַל־ אֲמָתֶ֔ךָ כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תֹּאמַ֥ר אֵלֶ֛יךָ שָׂרָ֖ה שְׁמַ֣ע בְּקֹלָ֑הּ כִּ֣י בְיִצְחָ֔ק יִקָּרֵ֥א לְךָ֖ זָֽרַע׃

passages.text: But I will also make a nation of the slave woman’s son, because he is your offspring.”
passages.sermon: God spoke to Abraham.\r\nGod said, “I will make the slave woman’s son into a nation.\r\nHe is your offspring.”
passages.original: וְגַ֥ם אֶת־ בֶּן־ הָאָמָ֖ה לְג֣וֹי אֲשִׂימֶ֑נּוּ כִּ֥י זַרְעֲךָ֖ הֽוּא׃

passages.text: Early in the morning, Abraham got up, took bread and a skin of water, put them on Hagar’s shoulders, and sent her away with the boy. She left and wandered in the Wilderness of Beersheba.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a servant of God.
Abraham got up early in the morning.
He took bread.
He took a skin of water.
He put the bread and the water on Hagar’s shoulders.
Hagar was his maidservant.
Abraham gave Hagar the boy.
The boy was her son.
Abraham sent Hagar and the boy away.
Hagar left.
She wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba.
passages.original: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֣ם אַבְרָהָ֣ם׀ בַּבֹּ֡קֶר וַיִּֽקַּֽח־ לֶחֶם֩ וְחֵ֨מַת מַ֜יִם וַיִּתֵּ֣ן אֶל־ הָ֠גָר שָׂ֧ם עַל־ שִׁכְמָ֛הּ וְאֶת־ הַיֶּ֖לֶד וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֶ֑הָ וַתֵּ֣לֶךְ וַתֵּ֔תַע בְּמִדְבַּ֖ר בְּאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע׃

passages.text: When the water in the skin was gone, she left the boy under one of the bushes.
passages.sermon:
Hagar was the mother of Abraham’s son Ishmael.
Hagar traveled in the wilderness with her son.
She carried a skin filled with water.
The water in the skin ran out.
Hagar had no more water for her son.
She placed the boy under one of the bushes.
passages.original: וַיִּכְל֥וּ הַמַּ֖יִם מִן־ הַחֵ֑מֶת וַתַּשְׁלֵ֣ךְ אֶת־ הַיֶּ֔לֶד תַּ֖חַת אַחַ֥ד הַשִּׂיחִֽם׃

passages.text: Then she went off and sat down nearby, about a bowshot away, for she said, “I cannot bear to watch the boy die!” And as she sat nearby, she lifted up her voice and wept.
passages.sermon:
Hagar was the mother of the boy.
She left the boy under a bush.
She walked away from him.
She sat down by herself.
She sat at a distance from the boy.
The distance was about as far as a bow can shoot an arrow.
She said, “I cannot watch the boy die.”
She sat at that distance.
She raised her voice.
She wept.
passages.original: וַתֵּלֶךְ֩ וַתֵּ֨שֶׁב לָ֜הּ מִנֶּ֗גֶד הַרְחֵק֙ כִּמְטַחֲוֵ֣י קֶ֔שֶׁת כִּ֣י אָֽמְרָ֔ה אַל־ אֶרְאֶ֖ה בְּמ֣וֹת הַיָּ֑לֶד וַתֵּ֣שֶׁב מִנֶּ֔גֶד וַתִּשָּׂ֥א אֶת־ קֹלָ֖הּ וַתֵּֽבְךְּ׃

passages.text: Then God heard the voice of the boy, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven, “What is wrong, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he lies.
passages.sermon:
God listened to the boy’s voice.
The boy was Ishmael, Hagar’s son.
God sent an angel.
The angel spoke from heaven.
The angel called to Hagar.
The angel said, “What is wrong, Hagar?”
The angel said, “Do not be afraid.”
The angel said, “God has heard the boy’s voice.”
The angel said, “God hears him where he is.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע אֱלֹהִים֮ אֶת־ ק֣וֹל הַנַּעַר֒ וַיִּקְרָא֩ מַלְאַ֨ךְ אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀ אֶל־ הָגָר֙ מִן־ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לָ֖הּ מַה־ לָּ֣ךְ הָגָ֑ר אַל־ תִּ֣ירְאִ֔י כִּֽי־ שָׁמַ֧ע אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶל־ ק֥וֹל הַנַּ֖עַר בַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הוּא־ שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: Get up, lift up the boy, and take him by the hand, for I will make him into a great nation.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Hagar.
God sent an angel from heaven.
The angel said, “Get up, Hagar.
Lift up the boy.
Take him by the hand.
I will make the boy into a great nation.”
passages.original: ק֚וּמִי שְׂאִ֣י אֶת־ הַנַּ֔עַר וְהַחֲזִ֥יקִי אֶת־ יָדֵ֖ךְ בּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־ לְג֥וֹי גָּד֖וֹל אֲשִׂימֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. So she went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink.
passages.sermon:
God acted with power and mercy.
God opened Hagar’s eyes.
Hagar saw a well of water.
Hagar went to the well.
She filled the skin with water.
She gave the boy water to drink.
passages.original: וַיִּפְקַ֤ח אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־ עֵינֶ֔יהָ וַתֵּ֖רֶא בְּאֵ֣ר מָ֑יִם וַתֵּ֜לֶךְ וַתְּמַלֵּ֤א אֶת־ הַחֵ֙מֶת֙ מַ֔יִם וַתַּ֖שְׁקְ אֶת־ הַנָּֽעַר׃

passages.text: And God was with the boy, and he grew up and settled in the wilderness and became a great archer.
passages.sermon:
God stayed with the boy.
The boy grew up.
The boy lived in the wilderness.
The boy became a skilled archer.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֧י אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת־ הַנַּ֖עַר וַיִּגְדָּ֑ל וַיֵּ֙שֶׁב֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וַיְהִ֖י רֹבֶ֥ה קַשָּֽׁת׃

passages.text: And while he was dwelling in the Wilderness of Paran, his mother got a wife for him from the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon: The boy lived in the Wilderness of Paran.\r\nHis mother chose a wife for him.\r\nShe found the wife in the land of Egypt.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בְּמִדְבַּ֣ר פָּארָ֑ן וַתִּֽקַּֽח־ ל֥וֹ אִמּ֛וֹ אִשָּׁ֖ה מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃פ

passages.text: At that time Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army said to Abraham, “God is with you in all that you do.
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was a king.
Phicol was the commander of Abimelech’s army.
Abraham was a man chosen by God.
At that time, Abimelech and Phicol spoke to Abraham.
They said these words to Abraham.
They said, “God is with you.”
They said, “God is with you in everything you do.”
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔וא וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֗לֶךְ וּפִיכֹל֙ שַׂר־ צְבָא֔וֹ אֶל־ אַבְרָהָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר אֱלֹהִ֣ים עִמְּךָ֔ בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ אַתָּ֖ה עֹשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: Now, therefore, swear to me here before God that you will not deal falsely with me or my children or descendants. Show to me and to the country in which you reside the same kindness that I have shown to you.”
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was the king of Gerar.
Phicol was the commander of Abimelech’s army.
Abimelech spoke to Abraham.
Abimelech said, “Swear to me here before God.
Promise that you will not lie to me.
Promise that you will not lie to my children.
Promise that you will not lie to my descendants.
I have shown kindness to you.
Show the same kindness to me.
Show the same kindness to the land where you live.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה הִשָּׁ֨בְעָה לִּ֤י בֵֽאלֹהִים֙ הֵ֔נָּה אִם־ תִּשְׁקֹ֣ר לִ֔י וּלְנִינִ֖י וּלְנֶכְדִּ֑י כַּחֶ֜סֶד אֲשֶׁר־ עָשִׂ֤יתִי עִמְּךָ֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה עִמָּדִ֔י וְעִם־ הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־ גַּ֥רְתָּה בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: And Abraham replied, “I swear it.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a man chosen by God.
Abraham spoke to Abimelech.
Abraham said, “I will swear.”
Abraham promised to do as Abimelech asked.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אַבְרָהָ֔ם אָנֹכִ֖י אִשָּׁבֵֽעַ׃

passages.text: But when Abraham complained to Abimelech about a well that Abimelech’s servants had seized, Abimelech replied, “I do not know who has done this. You did not tell me, so I have not heard about it until today.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a man chosen by God.
Abraham lived in the land of the Philistines.
Abimelech was the king of the Philistines.
Abraham spoke to Abimelech.
Abraham complained to Abimelech.
Abraham said that Abimelech’s servants had taken a well of water.
Abimelech answered Abraham.
Abimelech said, “I do not know who did this.”
Abimelech said, “You did not tell me.”
Abimelech said, “I have not heard about it until today.”
passages.original: וְהוֹכִ֥חַ אַבְרָהָ֖ם אֶת־ אֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ עַל־ אֹדוֹת֙ בְּאֵ֣ר הַמַּ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר גָּזְל֖וּ עַבְדֵ֥י אֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ׃ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי מִ֥י עָשָׂ֖ה אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וְגַם־ אַתָּ֞ה לֹא־ הִגַּ֣דְתָּ לִּ֗י וְגַ֧ם אָנֹכִ֛י לֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי בִּלְתִּ֥י הַיּֽוֹם׃

passages.text: So Abraham brought sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelech, and the two men made a covenant.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a man chosen by God.
Abraham took sheep and cattle.
Abraham gave the sheep and cattle to Abimelech.
Abimelech was a king.
Abraham and Abimelech made a covenant together.
A covenant is a solemn agreement.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֤ח אַבְרָהָם֙ צֹ֣אן וּבָקָ֔ר וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לַאֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ וַיִּכְרְת֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם בְּרִֽית׃

passages.text: Abraham separated seven ewe lambs from the flock, and Abimelech asked him, “Why have you set apart these seven ewe lambs?”
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a man chosen by God.
Abraham took seven ewe lambs from his flock.
He set these seven ewe lambs apart from the rest.
Abimelech was the king of Gerar.
Abimelech saw what Abraham did.
Abimelech spoke to Abraham.
Abimelech asked Abraham a question.
He said, “Why have you set apart these seven ewe lambs?”
passages.original: וַיַּצֵּ֣ב אַבְרָהָ֗ם אֶת־ שֶׁ֛בַע כִּבְשֹׂ֥ת הַצֹּ֖אן לְבַדְּהֶֽן׃ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ אֶל־ אַבְרָהָ֑ם מָ֣ה הֵ֗נָּה שֶׁ֤בַע כְּבָשֹׂת֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִצַּ֖בְתָּ לְבַדָּֽנָה׃

passages.text: He replied, “You are to accept the seven ewe lambs from my hand as my witness that I dug this well.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham spoke to Abimelech.
Abraham told Abimelech to take seven ewe lambs from his hand.
Abraham said these seven ewe lambs would be a witness for him.
The lambs would show that Abraham dug the well.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֚י אֶת־ שֶׁ֣בַע כְּבָשֹׂ֔ת תִּקַּ֖ח מִיָּדִ֑י בַּעֲבוּר֙ תִּֽהְיֶה־ לִּ֣י לְעֵדָ֔ה כִּ֥י חָפַ֖רְתִּי אֶת־ הַבְּאֵ֥ר הַזֹּֽאת׃

passages.text: So that place was called Beersheba, because it was there that the two of them swore an oath.
passages.sermon:
Abraham and Abimelech were present at a certain place.
They both swore an oath there.
People called that place Beersheba.
They called it Beersheba because the two men swore an oath there.
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּ֗ן קָרָ֛א לַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא בְּאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע כִּ֛י שָׁ֥ם נִשְׁבְּע֖וּ שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: After they had made the covenant at Beersheba, Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army got up and returned to the land of the Philistines.
passages.sermon:
Abraham and Abimelech made a covenant at Beersheba.
Phicol was the commander of Abimelech’s army.
Abimelech and Phicol stood up.
Abimelech and Phicol returned to the land of the Philistines.
passages.original: וַיִּכְרְת֥וּ בְרִ֖ית בִּבְאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע וַיָּ֣קָם אֲבִימֶ֗לֶךְ וּפִיכֹל֙ שַׂר־ צְבָא֔וֹ וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ אֶל־ אֶ֥רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

passages.text: And Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and there he called upon the name of the LORD, the Eternal God.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was in Beersheba.
Abraham planted a tamarisk tree there.
Abraham called on the name of the LORD in that place.
The LORD is the Eternal God.
passages.original: וַיִּטַּ֥ע אֶ֖שֶׁל בִּבְאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע וַיִּ֨קְרָא־ שָׁ֔ם בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֵ֥ל עוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: And Abraham resided in the land of the Philistines for a long time.
passages.sermon: Abraham lived in the land of the Philistines.\r\nHe stayed there for many days.
passages.original: וַיָּ֧גָר אַבְרָהָ֛ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים׃פ
